subject: Commit-to-Fleet scaling blueprint and cutover timeline
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novamedics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@novamedics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for Dedicated commit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. To recap — NovaMedics is ready to commit to a reserved pool but needs a concrete sizing and cutover plan we can use for internal procurement and change windows. Key asks from our side:

- A validated GPU count and rightsize for our peak 95th percentile traffic (we expect 280 concurrent sessions with avg sequence 512, estimated 2.5M tok/day initially).
- A pre-cutover validation window and acceptance tests we can run on our side (throughput, tails, latency SLOs).
- A cutover timeline that minimizes customer impact (preferred weekend blackout window) and clear rollback triggers.
- Estimated costs for the reserved tier vs hosted (first 6 months).

Could you put together a blueprint we can circulate internally? Procurement deadline is 2026-11-25, so we need something this week if possible.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a follow-up call.

Alex
VP, Platform Engineering
NovaMedics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novamedics.com>
Cc: eng-ops@novamedics.com, k arthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit-to-Fleet scaling blueprint and cutover timeline

Alex —

Thanks, this is helpful context. I pulled together a first-pass blueprint and an internal checklist for validation. High-level summary below, full attachments in Drive (listed at bottom).

Proposed approach (summary):
- Commit profile: Start with reserved pool of 8xA100-equivalent GPUs (mixed perf: 6 high-memory for large models + 2 throughput-optimized for embeddings). Headroom targets ~30% for peak growth month 1.
- Throughput validation window: 72-hour staged validation (50% traffic mirroring first 24h, then 100% synthetic load for 48h).
- Acceptance criteria: 95th pct latency < 250ms for <1s calls, tail 99.9% below 1200ms for generation up to 512 tokens; error rate <0.2% sustained.
- Cutover cadence: Two-week runway for preflight and dry runs, final weekend blackout (Sat 02:00–06:00 PT) for the swap. Rollback plan to unpin routing with 30-minute rollback SLA if error conditions met.
- Cost delta: Preliminary estimate attached (commit vs hosted) with monthly amortized GPU cost and predicted token unit cost.

Immediate asks for NovaMedics:
1) Confirm desired blackout window preference (the weekend above is our default).
2) Share top-10 golden prompts for quality regressions (we’ll wire them into the acceptance harness).
3) Sign off on embargoed dry-run dates (we suggest 11/28–11/30 for internal dry runs; final cutover weekend 12/04–12/05).

Internal notes: looping in Karthik and Monica to validate sizing and the acceptance checklist below. Ben — please flag any billing/pricing concerns for the proposal.

Attachments: commit-sizing-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet), cutover-runbook-draft.pdf, slo-acceptance-checklist.md
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0A1B2C3/commit-sizing-estimates

–Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: NovaMedics sizing validation & runbook (please review)

Team —

Forwarding Alex’s asks and the blueprint I shared. I want a quick internal alignment thread with clear owners so we can push a single doc to the customer by EOD 11/12. Please comment inline in the shared runbook or reply with your estimates. Key validation items where I need concrete numbers:

- Karthik: confirm GPU mix and 95th-percentile per-GPU QPS for the model family they plan to run (they flagged a mix of base Llama-derivatives + a condensed reranker). Also call out warm-up KV cache expectations for mirrored traffic.
- Monica: ops plan for a staged 72h validation (traffic mirroring + synthetic ramp); please include staffing + on-call cadence during the blackout.
- Ben: outline the pricing delta table and how we present the amortized cost over first 6 months; flag contractual minimums that apply to reserved capacity.

If we can get numbers by EOD tomorrow (11/12 COB), I’ll package and send to Alex for procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: NovaMedics sizing validation & runbook (please review)

Quick sizing notes after reviewing their telemetry sample and the sequence distribution they shared:

- Recommended starting reserve: 8 GPUs (6x80GB A100-class, 2x48GB T4-class equivalent for high-concurrency embedding paths). Rationale: model mix ~80% decoder Llama-derivative (prefers memory-heavy GPUs for kv cache), 20% short-embedding traffic.
- Perf expectations (conservative): per high-memory GPU sustained: ~18 concurrent 512-token generation sessions (avg infer cost ~0.42s/token pipeline, batching expected). That yields ~108 concurrent generation sessions on the 6 GPUs and ~48 embedding QPS capacity on the 2 throughput GPUs. Combined this meets the 280 concurrent projection with ~10–15% headroom.
- Batching note: recommend initial batching window 30ms, max batch 64 tokens; adaptive batching config attached in runbook.
- KV cache warm-up: expect 6–12 hour warm-up to hit steady-state for prefix-heavy traffic; mirror the last 48h of traffic for warm-up in preflight.
- Acceptance tests:
  * Throughput: sustained 95th percentile throughput at 85% of provisioned capacity for 4 consecutive hours during the 72h validation.
  * Latency: 95th < 250ms, 99.9th < 1200ms for seq<=512.
  * Error budget: <0.2% non-retryable failures.

I'll add detailed perf curves into commit-sizing-estimates.xlsx and mark the corners where we expect risk (KV warm-up and tails under heavy batching). If we want additional safety margin, increase the reserve to 10 GPUs (adds ~22% cost).

-Karthik
Principal Infra Performance Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: eng-ops@novamedics.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Commit-to-Fleet scaling blueprint and cutover timeline (proposal)

Alex —

Appended the internal validation inputs and Karthik’s sizing curves; attached is the consolidated blueprint and proposed timeline. TL;DR recommended plan below and asks to confirm by 11/22 so procurement can finalize before your 11/25 cutoff.

Recommended commit & timeline (final):
- Commit: 8 GPUs (6x80GB + 2x48GB throughput) with option to scale to 10 during onboarding if tails exceed expectations.
- Dry-run window (internal only): 2026-11-28 08:00 PT through 2026-11-30 20:00 PT — includes 24h mirrored traffic baseline and 48h synthetic stress.
- Final cutover weekend (customer-visible swap): 2026-12-04 02:00 PT – 2026-12-04 06:00 PT (preferred). We’ll run a quick smoke validation immediately after the swap and keep routing fallback for 4 hours.
- Rollback triggers: sustained >0.5% non-retryable errors for 30m, or 95th latency breach > +300ms for 20m. If triggered, automatic rollback to hosted routing and paging to the on-call infra lead (Monica).
- Acceptance checklist: please review the attached slo-acceptance-checklist.md; we’ll run the golden prompts you provide during the mirror window.
- Cost: see commit-sizing-estimates.xlsx for amortized monthly cost; preliminary delta shows ~18% reduction in per-token unit cost at the projected usage after amortization.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm blackout preference and sign-off on the dry-run dates (reply-all).
2) NovaMedics ops — upload top-10 golden prompts to the Drive link and grant our infra read-only access by 11/20.
3) Procurement — if you want alternate cutover weekend options we can accommodate 12/11 as a fallback.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/some/link/DEAL-4782 (proposal + reserved contract stub)
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0A1B2C3/commit-sizing-estimates

We’re ready to run the dry-runs as soon as we have your confirmation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
